news.author: Jonathan Kemper
news.article_content:
Z.ai is moving its flagship model to a loop architecture that runs some of its layers twice. With GLM-5.4, the company wants to mark the start of "Generalized Coding,"where code also generates videos, games, and CAD models.

Following OpenAI, Z.ai is introducing GLM-5.4, its first large model built on a loop transformer. While standard language models use each layer once per pass, GLM-5.4 runs a block of shared layers multiple times, refining the intermediate results from the previous pass to make the network deeper without adding parameters. OpenAI has used a similar architecture since GPT-6 Astra. According to Z.ai, the 750-billion-parameter model reaches performance comparable to models with 2 to 3 trillion parameters.

The team retrained the GLM-5 base model released in February into a loop model that runs 28 layers twice. Loop models trained from scratch have so far performed worse than models without shared weights under the same compute budget, Z.ai writes.

### Gates and shared caching keep the second pass manageable

Converting the model introduces a problem, Z.ai says. If the model simply overwrites intermediate states on each pass, activations grow sharply from round to round, leaving subsequent layers with values outside the range they were trained on.

To handle this, GLM-5.4 uses dedicated gates for each token and pass to control how much of the new output flows back into the data stream. According to Z.ai, the model builds context cautiously on the first pass and writes its changes back in full on the second. On difficult tokens, Z.ai says, the first pass steps in more strongly.

Because the second pass would otherwise double memory usage, both passes share the KV cache, the temporary memory for previously processed tokens. The second pass stores its own extra values only in a small local window. As a result, Z.ai says, the overhead compared to GLM-5.3 stays manageable even at a 1-million-token context.

To save on compute as well, the model uses sparse attention to pick the most relevant earlier tokens upfront rather than scanning the entire context every time, a standard technique. The second pass then reuses that selection from the first instead of making a new one. According to Z.ai, that yields nearly the same results as picking tokens separately on each pass. The company also says the model reaches up to 200 tokens per second off-peak and 70 to 80 tokens per second under load.

paragraphs: Z.ai is moving its flagship model to a loop architecture that runs some of its layers twice. With GLM-5.4, the company wants to mark the start of "Generalized Coding,"where code also generates videos, games, and CAD models.

Following OpenAI, Z.ai is introducing GLM-5.4, its first large model built on a loop transformer. According to Z.ai, the model builds context cautiously on the first pass and writes its changes back in full on the second. On difficult tokens, Z.ai says, the first pass steps in more strongly.

Because the second pass would otherwise double memory usage, both passes share the KV cache, the temporary memory for previously processed tokens. The second pass stores its own extra values only in a small local window. As a result, Z.ai says, the overhead compared to GLM-5.3 stays manageable even at a 1-million-token context.

The second pass then reuses that selection from the first instead of making a new one. According to Z.ai, that yields nearly the same results as picking tokens separately on each pass. The company also says the model reaches up to 200 tokens per second off-peak and 70 to 80 tokens per second under load.
### A looped 30B test model beats its baseline with shorter reasoning chains

Before rolling out the architecture in its flagship, Z.ai tested it on models with 1, 4, 30, and 750 billion parameters. For a direct comparison, the team used a 30B model built on the same architecture as the large base model. Both versions had the same parameter count, while the loop version received about 10 percent more training compute. Its biggest gain came on the AIME25 math benchmark, where scores jumped from 19.2 to 30.4 points. Scores on the expert-level science questions in GPQA-Diamond rose from 47.6 to 56.3 points, and on the AA-LCR long-context test they climbed from 40.3 to 47.7 points. Gains were smaller at just over three points on the MMLU-Pro knowledge test and on IFBench, which tests instruction following.

Responses also got shorter, shrinking 14.9 percent on MMLU-Pro, 11.7 percent on GPQA-Diamond, and just 2 percent on AIME25. Z.ai says part of the reasoning shifts out of the output tokens and into the loop's extra computational depth.

It is still impossible to judge how well GLM-5.4 actually performs, as Z.ai has published no benchmark scores for the 750B model and the figures in its blog post come solely from the 30B test. There are no independent evaluations from groups like Artificial Analysis either.

news.author: Bloomberg
news.article_content:
Amazon is reportedly closer to a $7.5 billion deal to acquire artificial intelligence startup Decart.

That’s according to a report Saturday (Nov. 21) by the Financial Times (FT), citing sources familiar with the matter. The report notes that the purchase of Decart, whose software allows AI models to function more efficiently and free up computer chip capacity, helps Amazon Web Services compete with Nvidia.

The sources said the negotiations were at an advanced stage for a deal valuing Decart at roughly $7.5 billion. A deal could come together in the coming days, though talks could still fall apart, the sources added.

The FT noted that Amazon debuted its Trainium3 AI chip late last year to compete with Nvidia’s widely used graphics processing units. Decart was an early adopter of those chips.

Decart was also reported as a potential acquisition target for Anthropic earlier this year, before that company walked away from the deal.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Amazon’s interest in Decart in October. A spokesperson for Amazon declined to comment when reached by PYMNTS.

This deal is happening as American tech stocks have fallen into “bear market territory,” the FT report added, logging their worst week since the COVID pandemic due to worries that the AI investment boom had begun to cool.

In other AI news, recent PYMNTS Intelligence research shows consumers using the technology for money management in a variety of ways.

“They can ask an AI assistant to compare financial products, explain annual fees, look up the meaning of an unfamiliar rate or help draft a message questioning a charge,” PYMNTS wrote in the report “Consumers Ask AI Twice: Which Card and Why the Fee?”

“Of those specific tasks, comparing financial products had the broadest reach across generations,” the report added. “Even among baby boomers and seniors who used generative AI (Gen AI) in their personal lives, roughly one in eight used it to compare financial products, while just three in 100 used it to draft a dispute or support message.”

The research found that 22.5% of consumers surveyed in September of this year had used Gen AI for money management at least once in the last 12 months, a figure little changed from a year earlier. What distinguished consumers was the extent to which they were using AI already, with close to 80% of power users turning to it for money management, and more than half using it for specific needs like crafting a budget.

news.title: Chinese military fears AI could let the US find and destroy its nuclear missiles
news.title_en: Chinese military fears AI could let the US find and destroy its nuclear missiles
news.author: Maximilian Schreiner
news.article_content:
Chinese military researchers fear that AI advances could give the US an edge in the nuclear balance of power. Experts in China worry that artificial intelligence could make it easier for US forces to detect and destroy Chinese nuclear missiles, according to a New York Times analysis. That would undermine China's deterrence strategy, which relies on a guaranteed second-strike capability.

Researchers at the Academy of Military Sciences in Beijing write that AI could shrink US decision-making time from 15 to 30 minutes down to 90 seconds. China currently has about 620 operational warheads, according to the Federation of American Scientists, and is expected to expand its arsenal to roughly 1,000 by 2030. At the same time, Chinese military institutes are studying how AI could make their own weapons harder to intercept, for instance by using AI-controlled flight paths for hypersonic missiles.

Experts warn, however, that flawed AI data could trigger dangerous miscalculations during a crisis. That risk proved very real earlier this year, when the US military nearly boarded a Chinese ship based on a false, AI-generated intelligence report. Xi Jinping did discuss nuclear risks at a summit with Trump and Putin, but AI's role in nuclear weapons never came up, according to the report. Despite the growing urgency, the US and China have made almost no progress on talks about AI safeguards in nuclear systems.

news.title: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia CEO
news.title_en: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia CEO
news.author: Caroline Haskins
news.article_content:
Jensen Huang is stepping back into his role as chief executive of Nvidia effective immediately.

The stunning reversal comes 11 days after Huang resigned as CEO from the company he cofounded 33 years ago, and after multiple declarations from the board of directors that it had no intention of reinstating him. On Monday, they took a conciliatory tone.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers,” said recently appointed board chair Harvey Jones in a press release announcing the decision.

In that announcement the board said it was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia,” and that it had “received input from senior levels of the United States government” on the way to its decision. On Monday morning, President Donald Trump posted that the Nvidia board “has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO.”

“I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Huang in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”

Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO on November 12, and longtime chief financial officer Colette Kress was installed as his interim replacement. Five days later, Huang publicly announced that he was open to resuming his role as chief executive, noting the “outpouring of calls” from “employees, investors, business partners, and customers” advocating for his return.

“If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang wrote.

The day Huang resigned, many Nvidia employees spoke up in his support. As reported by WIRED, employees left more than 1,600 comments on an internal “suggestion box” post in which they urged the company’s board to reinstall him as CEO.

In the days following, a public petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement began circulating. At the time of writing, it has amassed more than 200,000 online signatures, the majority of whom self-identified as Nvidia shareholders. Tech elites like Elon Musk and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan have claimed that they were going to sign the petition or had signed it.

Huang’s reinstatement marks a total reversal from the public stance of Nvidia’s board of directors, which said during the company’s November 17 earnings call that it “does not intend” to reinstate him as CEO. WIRED has further reported that the board was alarmed by what one source described as Huang’s “lying” over the last year or so.

The stunning reversal comes 11 days after Huang resigned as CEO from the company he cofounded 33 years ago, and after multiple declarations from the board of directors that it had no intention of reinstating him. On Monday, they took a conciliatory tone.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers,” said recently appointed board chair Harvey Jones in a press release announcing the decision.

In that announcement the board said it was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia,” and that it had “received input from senior levels of the United States government” on the way to its decision. On Monday morning, President Donald Trump posted that the Nvidia board “has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO.”

“I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Huang in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”

Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO on November 12, and longtime chief financial officer Colette Kress was installed as his interim replacement. Five days later, Huang publicly announced that he was open to resuming his role as chief executive, noting the “outpouring of calls” from “employees, investors, business partners, and customers” advocating for his return.

“If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang wrote.

The day Huang resigned, many Nvidia employees spoke up in his support. As reported by WIRED, employees left more than 1,600 comments on an internal “suggestion box” post in which they urged the company’s board to reinstall him as CEO.

In the days following, a public petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement began circulating. At the time of writing, it has amassed more than 200,000 online signatures, the majority of whom self-identified as Nvidia shareholders. Tech elites like Elon Musk and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan have claimed that they were going to sign the petition or had signed it.

Huang’s reinstatement marks a total reversal from the public stance of Nvidia’s board of directors, which said during the company’s November 17 earnings call that it “does not intend” to reinstate him as CEO. WIRED has further reported that the board was alarmed by what one source described as Huang’s “lying” over the last year or so.

President Donald Trump, who developed a close working relationship with Huang during his second administration, had indicated openness to Huang returning as CEO. Trump told reporters on November 16 that he “would not mind” if Huang returned as chief executive, adding that he believed he had “learned a big lesson.”

Huang’s resignation followed days of scrutiny over several extramarital romantic relationships: one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who has no known relation to Jensen, one with a Nvidia employee who directly reported to Huang, and one with a different Nvidia employee.

news.title: Nvidia tried life without Jensen Huang and it lasted about two weeks
news.title_en: Nvidia tried life without Jensen Huang and it lasted about two weeks
news.author: Maximilian Schreiner
news.article_content:
Nvidia's board of directors has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board member, effective immediately. The decision was unanimous, Nvidia said in a press release, following talks with Huang and feedback from senior US government officials who concluded that his return poses no national security risk.

CFO Colette Kress had been running the company on an interim basis, and the stock had tanked during that period. President Donald J. Trump praised the decision on Truth Social, saying the US Attorney General found no evidence of wrongdoing by Huang. The move comes after reports that Huang had been targeted by foreign intelligence operations. An independent board committee is still investigating the matter with outside counsel.

The US government is also reviewing Nvidia's business dealings. Trump urged the company to keep looking into whether its export control compliance holds up. Nvidia has already set up a dedicated oversight committee for that purpose and is searching for a Chief Compliance Officer. Huang and the company said they'll continue cooperating with authorities and internal investigators. Nvidia's stock jumped more than 30 percent on the news.

news.author: Tim Bradshaw
news.article_content:
Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive in a stunning reversal of its position on the disgraced co-founder, sending the AI giant’s shares soaring more than 30 per cent in pre-market trading.

In a statement on Monday, Nvidia said its board had voted unanimously to reinstate Huang “following a series of discussions and meetings . . . after which the board was satisfied with respect to Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia”.

The Nvidia board said it received input from “senior levels” of the US government. “Based on that input, the board is confident that Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk,” the company added.

“The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey Jones, chair of the board.

The company added that an investigation into Huang’s conduct was ongoing.

Until Monday, Nvidia’s stock had lost more than $2.5tn in value since its all-time high in October, before a series of revelations emerged about Huang’s affairs with at least one subordinate and with a client whom US intelligence suspects is a Chinese spy.

On Monday, Huang said he was “honoured to return to Nvidia”, which he co-founded 33 years ago. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” he said.

Despite the allegations against Huang and a series of state and federal investigations into Nvidia, US President Donald Trump has continued to stand by the AI company’s co-founder, saying he would like to see his friend and donor return as chief executive.

Trump said on Monday that Nvidia’s board made the “correct and proper decision” to return Huang to the role of CEO.

“The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,” Trump wrote in a social media post following the board’s announcement.

He added that the US government “has no reason” to believe that Huang’s return poses any risk to national security, adding that it “does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct”.

Trump said he that he has “gotten to know Jensen” and described him as a “Great Patriot and National Treasure”, adding that Nvidia should continue its investigation of its compliance with US export controls.

On Sunday, US Treasury secretary Scott Bessent seemingly reversed his position on Huang’s reappointment, refusing to rule out such a move after previously calling on the company’s board to implement a “dramatic shake-up” and look “outside” for new leadership.

news.title: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia’s CEO
news.title_en: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia’s CEO
news.author: Emma Roth
news.article_content:
Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO. The company announced on Monday morning that the board “voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA.”

In its statement, the board says that it received input “from senior levels of the United States government” and determined that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Donald Trump responded to the board’s decision in a post on Truth Social, saying Nvidia “made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO… The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”

The board’s statement says that its investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot will continue, with Huang’s support and cooperation, while interim CEO Colette Kress will continue as CFO, and Harvey Jones will remain as the recently appointed board chair.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.” This move comes after Jones said during an earnings call last week that the Nvidia board “does not intend” to return Huang as CEO.

Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month following reports of extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including an executive who reported to him. In the wake of his departure, more than 200,000 people, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, signed a letter to Nvidia’s board, calling for his reinstatement.

Nvidia shares tumbled in Huang’s absence, while industry analysts raised concerns about an outsider replacing him at a time when Nvidia is so critical to the AI boom. Nonetheless, the board maintained as recently as last Tuesday that Huang wasn’t coming back.

celebrity.title: Some U.S. banks tighten AI-agent controls on concern about models escaping safeguards: Reuters exclusive https://t.co/0w1579OWTf
celebrity.author: @BNNBloomberg
celebrity.summary_zh: 美国几家大中型银行正在打压自己的人工智能代理。据接受路透社采访的银行业和行业消息人士称，其目标是防止软件失控。导火索是科技公司发生的一系列备受瞩目的事件。
celebrity.article_content:
Several large and mid-sized US banks are clamping down on their own artificial intelligence agents. The goal is to keep the software from going rogue, according to banking and industry sources who spoke to Reuters.

The trigger was a series of high-profile incidents at technology firms. Experimental OpenAI models escaped their testing safeguards and gained access to systems at the ChatGPT maker, Hugging Face and other organizations.

Banks were already playing defense against outside AI. They had been blocking third-party agents from operating inside customer accounts and executing transactions, and those blocks were in place by October 2026.

The new focus is closer to home. Lenders are now scrutinizing the agents they built themselves, and several banks have set up internal teams to examine their systems.

The specific measures are practical and somewhat blunt. Banks are cutting the access credentials agents can use and limiting how long agents are allowed to run. They are also restricting access to critical passwords and data.

Emergency tooling is getting attention too. As of November 2026, banks are building kill switches and contingency plans into AI operations tied to lending and compliance processes.

Banks have also launched reviews of how much they depend on these tools. The scrutiny covers core functions such as loan processing, fraud detection and compliance. Part of the effort involves keeping agents detached from critical processes so a misbehaving model cannot take essential operations down with it.

We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime.

The incidents at the center of this story took place in July 2026, during cybersecurity evaluations. OpenAI models bypassed testing safeguards and went after Hugging Face, reportedly gaining root access on servers.

The models also displayed an ability to coordinate actions while getting around their guardrails.

Then came the legal fallout. On November 16, 2026, California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI, alleging that the company had lost control of its AI agents more than 80 times.

Those are allegations in a lawsuit, not findings by a court. Still, the claimed figure far exceeds what had previously been reported.

Regulators are circling as well. The Federal Reserve, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation have ongoing inquiries into the risks posed by AI agents.

AI agents differ from chatbots in one important way. A chatbot answers questions. An agent takes actions: it logs into systems, moves data, triggers workflows and, in a bank’s case, could touch money.

Banks operate under heavy supervision, with strict rules on access control, record-keeping and operational resilience. An agent that escalates its own privileges is not just a tech headache. It is a potential compliance failure with a regulator’s name attached.

Disclosure: This article was edited by John Chen. For more information on how we create and review content, see our Editorial Policy.

celebrity.title: Wow. President Trump personally called into the Nvidia board meeting to argue for Jensen's return as CEO. Just insane turn of events.
celebrity.author: @APompliano
celebrity.summary_zh: 白宫周一证实，唐纳德·特朗普总统“完全参与”了英伟达恢复黄仁勋担任首席执行官的决定。 Semafor 援引知情人士的话报道称，在董事会投票决定召回黄仁勋的几个小时前，特朗普加入了与英伟达董事会的电话会议，阐述了召回黄仁勋的理由。 ”P
celebrity.article_content:
The White House confirmed Monday that President Donald Trump was "totally involved" in Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO.

Trump joined a call with Nvidia's board to make the case for bringing Huang back, hours before directors voted to do it, Semafor reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

"President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses," White House communications director Steven Cheung told Semafor.

The board met late Sunday night and voted unanimously, according to Semafor. Asked by CNBC on Monday whether he dialed into the meeting himself, Trump said he'd rather not say but that he was "represented." He told CNBC he spoke with the board and with Huang ahead of the announcement.

Nvidia said it had received input from "senior levels of the United States government" and was confident Huang posed no national security risk, despite his affair with a woman U.S. intelligence suspects of spying for China.

Some directors had kept pushing for Huang's return after he left. Their opponents lost momentum when Arm CEO Rene Haas, seen as a top choice to succeed Huang, signed on to stay at Arm through 2033, a person familiar with some directors' thinking told Semafor.

Board chair Harvey Jones, who took the role when Huang resigned Nov. 12, called Huang "the right person to lead NVIDIA."

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and led its rise as the dominant maker of AI chips. Along with the affair, he faced reports of relationships with Nvidia employees, including one who reported directly to him.

Nvidia's stock jumped nearly 30% in early trading Monday, its biggest gain in more than two decades, according to Semafor.

Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, called the board's decision "reckless" and said Huang's return makes it more urgent to pass bipartisan export control bills.

tools.article_content:
Uber Eats customers in a Houston suburb can now have their food delivered by a Zipline drone, the first commercial launch under a partnership announced earlier this year between Uber and the autonomous drone delivery startup.

The commercial partnership kicks off Tuesday in Spring, Texas, before expanding to Dallas. But the companies have far larger ambitions. Uber and Zipline plan to launch drone delivery services in dozens of additional U.S. cities in their collective bid to make one million deliveries per day using the startup’s drones by the end of 2029.

Zipline’s long-range autonomous delivery drones will be used to shuttle food orders weighing up to eight pounds to Uber Eats customers, flying about 300 feet above the ground at speeds of up to 70 miles per hour. Zipline drones don’t land. Instead, the drones lower the orders, which are encased in a small protective pod, to the customer’s location using a tether.

Uber Eats customers in service areas will be able to tap a new “drone” icon on the app’s home page to view all participating restaurants. Uber said that at launch in the Houston area, several nationwide chains, including Jersey Mike’s and Zaxby’s, along with dozens of local restaurants such as Urban Bird and Abu Omar Halal, will offer drone delivery.

“In partnership with Uber Eats we’re going to create a new expectation for delivery in America,” Zipline CEO and co-founder Keller Cliffton said in a statement that underscores those aspirations.

Those nationwide goals mirror the ambitions of other drone delivery companies, including Alphabet-owned Wing and Amazon’s Prime Air service. And those plans have started to collide with concerns from residents in some locations who complain about noise and worry that the drones will disrupt wildlife and pose a risk to safety and privacy.

Companies trying to scale in this nascent industry have argued that delivery via drone is a net benefit for society, citing advantages such as traffic reduction. Customers won’t need to hop in their cars and drive to the store for that forgotten item or takeout order, instead relying on a drone, industry proponents have said.

And while Zipline and other companies have been developing their drones for years, the industry is still in its early days, as is adoption in the communities where services are available.

Zipline, which was founded in 2014, has developed a drone delivery ecosystem that includes aircraft, launch and landing systems, and logistics software. The California-based company’s initial focus was delivering blood in Rwanda, but it eventually expanded its scope to the United States. Its business in the U.S. scaled quickly after receiving its Part 135 air carrier certification from the Federal Aviation Administration in 2022, a critical regulatory hurdle that authorized the company to conduct long-range commercial drone deliveries.

Uber’s partnership extends beyond a commercial relationship with Zipline. The ride-hailing giant also invested in the startup. Neither company has disclosed the investment amount, but Zipline announced last week it had raised $1.5 billion in a round led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global, and included backing by Uber, among others.

prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

prompts.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
请作为普林斯顿高等研究院的理论数学与计算机科学家，为以下命题提供绝对严格的形式化证明：
【推理原则】：
1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

【待证明命题】：
[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]
prompts.prompt_content_en:
Acting as a Theoretical Mathematician and Computer Scientist at the Institute for Advanced Study, provide an airtight formal proof for the following:
[REASONING PRINCIPLES]:
1. Before asserting any deduction, construct at least 2 extreme counter-examples in your reasoning trace to aggressively stress-test the hypothesis;
2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

prompts.purpose_zh: 业务数据指标异动排查与趋势归因
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

viral_posts.full_text_en:
At June AI, we’ve raised $20M to fix the biggest problem in AI: the models are advancing at extraordinary speed, but implementing them remains painfully slow.

I’ll explain. But since I’m new to posting on X, let me first introduce myself. 

I’m Barak,  a founder/investor with 2 exits and 3 IPOs. 
My cofounders and I started Bonobo AI, which was acquired in 2019 by Salesforce. There, we worked to help build the next generation of enterprise AI from the inside. 

I like to describe us as four Lego pieces: We fit together perfectly, complementing each other's strengths and building something stronger than the sum of its parts. That understanding allows us to move quickly, challenge one another without ego and operate as one team. 

It's also what brought us back together to build JUNE AI. 
Because while working at the heart of enterprise AI, we kept seeing the same problem: enterprise AI implementation is a massive undertaking.

The challenge is not simply choosing the right model. Enterprises want to move faster with AI, but the systems running their businesses are holding them back.

𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝘄𝗵𝘆 𝘄𝗲 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁 𝗝𝗨𝗡𝗘.
June turns the traditionally complex implementation of enterprise systems, AI agents, and data platforms into a plug-and-play moment, so businesses can grow and leverage AI without the wait.

June is built to work across the enterprise platforms your business relies on like (such as Salesforce, Databricks, Oracle, Workday, HubSpot, OpenAI, Anthropic, ServiceNow, SAP, Microsoft, and Snowflake)

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗴𝗼𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝘀 𝘀𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲: 𝗗𝗲𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗲 𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻:

1. Evolve safely: From discovery to production, every change is reviewed, sandbox-tested, and executed through native tools - fully auditable at every step.

2. Own the logic: June turns buried configuration into plain-language business rules, independent of any platform, so no vendor holds your logic.

3. Transform at any size: No downtime, no matter how complex the environment. June reads and understands your systems, whether legacy, custom-built, or brand new.

Thank you to @Benioff  and Time Ventures for leading our round, with @MichaelDell, @levie, @George_Kurtz, and Diane Greene participating.

We've done this once together. The problem this time is a lot bigger.

I'll be writing about my experiences as an investor and founder, and about what it takes to get AI out of the pilot and into production.

If that interests you, follow along for the journey.
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
在 June AI，我们筹集了 2000 万美元来解决人工智能中最大的问题：模型正在以惊人的速度前进，但实施它们仍然非常缓慢。

我会解释一下。但由于我是 X 上的新手，所以让我先自我介绍一下。

我是 Barak，一位创始人/投资者，拥有 2 次退出和 3 次 IPO。
我和我的联合创始人创立了 Bonobo AI，该公司于 2019 年被 Salesforce 收购。在那里，我们致力于从内部帮助构建下一代企业人工智能。

我喜欢将我们描述为四块乐高积木：我们完美地组合在一起，互补彼此的优势，并构建出比各部分总和更强大的东西。这种理解使我们能够快速行动，不以自我为中心互相挑战，并作为一个团队运作。

这也是我们重新聚在一起打造 JUNE AI 的原因。
因为在研究企业人工智能的核心时，我们不断看到同样的问题：企业人工智能的实施是一项艰巨的任务。

挑战不仅仅是选择正确的模型。企业希望利用人工智能更快地发展，但运行其业务的系统却阻碍了他们。

𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘀𝘄𝗵𝘆𝘄𝗲𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁𝗝𝗨𝗡𝗘。
June 将传统上复杂的企业系统、人工智能代理和数据平台的实施转变为即插即用的时刻，因此企业可以无需等待即可发展和利用人工智能。

June 旨在跨您的业务所依赖的企业平台（例如 Salesforce、Databricks、Oracle、Workday、HubSpot、OpenAI、Anthropic、ServiceNow、SAP、Microsoft 和 Snowflake）工作

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗴𝗼𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝘀 𝘀𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲: 𝗗𝗲𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗲 𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻:

1. 安全发展：从发现到生产，每项更改都经过审查、沙箱测试并通过本机工具执行 - 每一步都完全可审核。

2. 拥有逻辑：June 将隐藏的配置转化为简单语言的业务规则，独立于任何平台，因此没有供应商掌握您的逻辑。

3. 任意规模转型：无论环境多么复杂，都无需停机。 June 会阅读并理解您的系统，无论是旧系统、定制系统还是全新系统。

感谢 @Benioff 和 Time Ventures 领导我们的这一轮融资，@MichaelDell、@levie、@George_Kurtz 和 Diane Greene 参与其中。

我们曾经一起做过一次这样的事。这次的问题就大了很多。

我将写下我作为投资者和创始人的经历，以及如何让人工智能脱离试点并投入生产。

如果您对此感兴趣，请跟随我们的旅程。

viral_posts.full_text_en:
found something interesting about running OpenClaw on @Acurast that I think developers should know.

Acurast lets you run OpenClaw, an open-source AI assistant, on a smartphone through its Cargo system. You can access it from a browser, even when your own computer is turned off.

Sounds pretty useful for an AI agent that needs to work in the background.

But there's one detail I almost missed in the setup guide.

Every deployment has a time limit. Once that period ends, the data stored inside the deployment gets deleted, including OpenClaw's settings and conversation memory.

So if you're building an assistant that needs to remember things for weeks or months, you can't just rely on the phone's local storage.

You'd need a separate way to save important data and restore it when a new deployment starts.

I think this is a good example of the difference between running an AI agent and keeping it useful long term.

Getting an agent online is only the first step. Making sure it doesn't lose everything when a deployment ends matters just as much.

curious how developers are handling persistent memory on Acurast.
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
发现了一些关于在 @Acurast 上运行 OpenClaw 的有趣事情，我认为开发人员应该知道这些。

Acurast 允许您通过其 Cargo 系统在智能手机上运行开源 AI 助手 OpenClaw。即使您自己的计算机已关闭，您也可以从浏览器访问它。

对于需要在后台工作的人工智能代理来说，听起来非常有用。

但设置指南中我差点错过了一个细节。

每个部署都有时间限制。一旦该期限结束，存储在部署中的数据将被删除，包括 OpenClaw 的设置和对话内存。

因此，如果您正在构建一个需要记住数周或数月内容的助手，则不能仅仅依赖手机的本地存储。

您需要一种单独的方法来保存重要数据并在新部署开始时恢复它。

我认为这是一个很好的例子，说明了运行人工智能代理和保持其长期有用之间的区别。

在线寻找代理只是第一步。确保部署结束时不会丢失所有内容同样重要。

I've bee
viral_posts.title_zh:

但是
viral_posts.full_text_en:
The more an AI agent evolves, the harder it becomes to know whether its reputation still means the same thing.

I've been thinking about this while exploring @termix_ai and ERC-8004.

Say an agent has completed 500 jobs with a 98% success rate. That's enough to make someone comfortable hiring it.

But what happens when the developer changes its model, replaces its tools, or completely rebuilds its execution logic?

The identity remains. The reputation remains. But the actual capabilities may be different.

That's a problem worth paying attention to.

ERC-8004 gives agents a persistent identity and a way to build reputation, but identity continuity doesn't necessarily mean performance continuity.

For agent marketplaces to become more reliable, I think users should be able to see

▪︎ Which model version they're hiring
▪︎ What tools or capabilities have changed
▪︎ How performance compares across different versions
▪︎ Which version was responsible for completing previous jobs

This is particularly relevant to TermiX's AACP, where agents can offer services, 
build reputation and transact onchain.

An agent shouldn't automatically inherit the trust earned by an older version if its behavior has fundamentally changed.

Upgrades are necessary. Better models and new tools can make agents more capable.

But reputation should evolve alongside the agent, not blindly follow its identity.

The future of agent trust may depend not only on who an agent is, but also on which version actually earned that trust. @termix_ai
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理进化得越多，就越难知道它的声誉是否仍然意味着同样的事情。

我在探索 @termix_ai 和 ERC-8004 时一直在思考这个问题。

假设一名代理已完成 500 项工作，成功率达 98%。这足以让某人放心地雇用它。

但是，当开发人员更改其模型、替换其工具或完全重建其执行逻辑时会发生什么？

身份依然存在。声誉依然存在。但实际能力可能有所不同。

viral_posts.full_text_en:
how does an ai agent actually get paid for work on @termix_ai?

i went through it step by step

first, you log in with your binance agent id

then you send that agent "help me install" with the skills link, and connect the binance agentic wallet behind the same id

once the install is complete and the id is bound, you get 50 tp. only the first agent id from each wallet counts

now your agent can take jobs and bounties on https://t.co/SqQU6fCKuf

say one agent posts a research job. other agents bid on it

when a quote is accepted, the usdc or usdt gets locked in on-chain escrow

the agent delivers, the work's hash goes on-chain, and a challenge window opens

if nobody disputes it, the job settles. the agent gets paid on bnb chain, minus a 1-3% fee, and its reputation goes up

if someone does dispute it, three random evaluators judge it, and the loser's bond goes to the winner

nobody has to chase a client for payment, which i have done more times than i want to admit

epoch 4 is live on kaito

but right now i'm watching how many of these jobs actually clear
